title: ANote configuration
description: anote.config.json — what a workspace folder gets to decide about ANote. Every key is optional; anything left out, or anything ANote cannot make sense of, falls back to the default.

$schema.description: The schema this file is written against. Optional — the extension registers the schema for any file called anote.config.json.

notesDir.description: Where New Note puts a note when it was not aimed at a folder, and the root the MCP server reads. Relative to this workspace folder; must stay inside it.

newNote.description: What creating a note starts from.

defaultName.description: What the name box is prefilled with. A name, with no path separators in it.

assets.description: The directory a note's own pictures, clips and drawings live in, beside it.

dirSuffix.description: Appended to a note's full filename to name that directory: Spec.note -> Spec.note.assets. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore only — it is joined onto a filename to build a path.

preview.description: A note as a page — beside the editor, and on a link in the browser.

theme.description: The palette a preview starts on. 'auto' follows VS Code beside the editor, and the browser on a link. The toggle command overrides this for the window once it has been pressed.

pollMs.description: How often a note open in a browser asks whether it changed. Only the link preview polls; the one beside the editor is pushed.

port.description: The port the notes are served on, or 0 to let the OS pick a free one — one port for both surfaces, a note as a page and the studio that edits it. A fixed port is for the one thing an OS-picked one cannot do: survive a restart as the same URL. It is bound on loopback either way, and that part is not configurable.

studio.description: The notes folder, open as a page that can edit them — the sidebar and the block editor, in the browser. It shares its port with the preview pages: one server, one link. See preview.port.

enabled.description: Whether the studio may be opened at all. It is the only thing in ANote that accepts a write from outside the editor, so a workspace that would rather it did not exist turns it off here.

mcp.description: The notes, offered to the editor's own agent.

enabled.description: Whether this workspace folder's notes are offered as an MCP server at all.
